question: does a sibling rebuild of the published hydrated recipe land inside the published fidelity interval?

verdict.sibling_mean_inside_published_interval_n: a weak check kept for completeness: the published interval is a bootstrap over source clusters of ONE model's per-context means, so it describes corpus sampling, not run-to-run spread. The paired interval is the test.
verdict.tie_convention: `fidelity.py paired` counts strict improvements as a_wins and the remainder as b_wins, so an exact tie is scored as a b-win. The three-way recount below comes from the same per-context means the paired tool subtracted.

what_a_sibling_must_reproduce: composition: every role's module count and storage formats
declared widths: bits, head_bits, mtp_bits, codebook, out_scales, calibration
the ten per-role byte totals and the total payload bytes
physical and logical tensor counts and the tensor_storage table
per shard: tensor names, dtypes, shapes, data offsets and the shard's size

recipe.sibling: MLP gate/up K5, down K6, attention K6 serialized (calibrated), lm_head K6/mcg, quantized MTP, BF16 embed+vision

command.sibling: convert.py -i Qwen3.8-27B -b 4 -hb 6 -mb 4 -vb 16 -cb mcg with EXL3_BITS_FIXED attention=6 and EXL3_BITS_OVERRIDE mlp gate/up=5 down=6

reference_capture_interchangeability.why: the published ladder deleted its BF16 capture after verifying its reports, so this run replayed against a surviving capture of the same reference. That is only sound if the two are interchangeable, which this control measures.
reference_capture_interchangeability.conclusion: the reference capture used for the sibling returns the published number, to every digit, for the published checkpoint: the reference swap is a no-op

protocol.note: the published number and the sibling's number are the same measurement run twice with one operand swapped: same v5 shard-0 suite, same BF16 reference content, same shared head, same comparator, same 512 contexts and 1,048,064 scored positions. The reference capture DIRECTORY differs, because the published ladder deleted its own; reference_capture_interchangeability measures that this is a no-op.

paired_aggregate.scope: v5 shard 0 only: 512 contexts, 1,048,064 scored positions

method.statistic: mean over contexts of (candidate A mean KLD - candidate B mean KLD)
method.interval: source-cluster bootstrap, 10,000 resamples, seed 1, 330 clusters resampled with replacement
method.operands: both candidates replayed through the same shared BF16 LM head; body-only, no candidate head quantization counted

scale.why: a converter draw only matters if it is comparable to a distinction we draw conclusions from. These are published paired margins at the identical resolution, so the ratio is directly meaningful.

capture_noise_floor.what: the same published checkpoint captured and replayed a SECOND time, paired against the published report
capture_noise_floor.why_it_matters: this comparison's floor is exactly zero, not a tolerance: recapture reproduces the published mean bitwise, so any nonzero paired difference measured against a sibling is attributable to the sibling's weights and to nothing in the capture or replay path.

what_this_run_did: converted the PUBLISHED hydrated recipe a second time, on the rental card, with the toolchain receipts/converter-determinism.json measured as the working one
verified the result is a SIBLING (identical recipe, different trellis payloads) rather than a twin or a different recipe
captured it on v5 shard 0 and replayed it against the published BF16 reference through the shared head, with the identical protocol the published number used
paired it per context against the published shard-0 report

What finalize adds is quantization_manifest.json, SHA256SUMS, DOCS-SHA256SUMS and build-receipt.json; it rewrites quantization_config.json only to add missing exl3 tensor_storage entries.

sibling_capture.tier: PRESERVE (tools/preserve_artifacts.sh tier 2, case (b): an input ceases to exist, so it cannot be regenerated at all)
sibling_capture.what: the hydrated SIBLING's hidden states over v5 shard 0, 512 contexts of 2,047 scored rows at hidden size 5,120, bfloat16
sibling_capture.verification: --deep: 507 files checked against the Hub's LFS oid (sha256 of the full bytes), 1 non-LFS file and 5 spot-checked LFS files re-downloaded and re-hashed from what the CDN actually serves. All 513 verified.
sibling_capture.full_inventory: /var/tmp/work/kld8/preserved-capture-sibling.json (per-file sha256, git blob id, bytes and check kind)
sibling_capture.why_preserved_rather_than_recomputed: the capture itself is about 6 minutes of GPU, which alone would put it in the state-the-cost tier. What moves it to PRESERVE is that recomputing it requires the sibling CHECKPOINT, and re-running the conversion does not reproduce that checkpoint -- it produces a THIRD distinct sibling, which is the finding of receipts/converter-determinism.json. So once the local checkpoint goes, this capture is the only surviving object from which the number in this receipt can be recomputed, and it is not reproducible at any price.

sibling_checkpoint.recompute_cost: about 40 minutes of GPU on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition for the conversion, plus its compile and finalize chain. This run measured 2,371.91 s (39.5 min) of converter-timed blocks and about 40 min of wall clock, and it completed on the first attempt because receipts/converter-determinism.json had already paid to discover which two steps need marisa_trie.
sibling_checkpoint.and_recomputing_it_does_not_reproduce_it: a re-run yields a different sibling, so the 40 minutes buys a NEW draw from the converter, not this one. The recompute cost of THIS checkpoint is therefore infinite; 40 minutes is the cost of another sample from the same distribution.
sibling_checkpoint.not_published_because: the measurement came back INDISTINGUISHABLE from the published checkpoint, which makes the sibling uninteresting as an artifact: it is 21.6 GB whose entire content as evidence is that it scored the same, and that fact is in this receipt together with the digests of all 16 of its files and the names of all 399 tensors that differ. Publishing a second checkpoint indistinguishable from the first would invite readers to download 21.6 GB to learn nothing, and would add a second artifact that our SHA256SUMS do not pin. Had the result been distinguishable the checkpoint would have been the evidence and would have had to be published.
sibling_checkpoint.what_survives_it: its per-file sha256 digests and the full list of differing tensors in this receipt's `siblinghood` block, its capture (preserved above, and sufficient to recompute the score without the weights), and its conversion log at /var/tmp/work/kld8/convert-hyd-sibling.log.

reference_capture_reused.verified_here: all 512 hidden files re-hashed against the capture manifest before the replay: 10,732,224,512 B, zero mismatches. The harness re-verifies every digest again on the way in and fails closed.
reference_capture_reused.not_re_uploaded_because: it is unchanged and already published; this run consumed it.

this_run.plain: A sibling rebuild lands inside the published fidelity interval. The paired 95 % interval on the per-context difference contains zero, so at this protocol's resolution -- 512 contexts, 1,048,064 scored positions, a source-cluster bootstrap over 330 clusters with 10,000 resamples at seed 1 -- the published checkpoint and a sibling of it are the same measurement.
for_every_published_fidelity_number: Unchanged, and now for a second reason. Every published number was already a measurement of the PUBLISHED bytes, which is what SHA256SUMS pins and what a downloader receives; that never depended on this test.

What this adds is the reconstruction claim receipts/converter-determinism.json had to leave as an expectation: 'rebuild this recipe and you will land on our numbers' is now measured, on one sibling, at this resolution. It is a tested expectation, not an identity -- the bytes still differ.
No extra variance term has to be added to any published interval, and no published claim needs amending.
what_it_does_not_license: It is one sibling, not a distribution. A single paired comparison bounds the converter's fidelity variance at this resolution; it does not estimate it.
It says nothing about recipes other than the hydrated one, nor about resolutions finer than this protocol's, nor about the tail statistics, which are reported here but were not the test.

the_other_outcome_would_have_meant.plain: A sibling rebuild does NOT land inside the published fidelity interval. The paired 95 % interval on the per-context difference excludes zero, so converter nondeterminism is fidelity-relevant: which of two equally valid solutions to the same recipe a conversion happens to find changes the measured distributional fidelity by an amount this protocol can see.
for_every_published_fidelity_number: Still correct as measurements OF THE PUBLISHED BYTES: they describe the artifact a downloader gets, and SHA256SUMS pins it. Nothing published becomes wrong.

But every one of them now carries a SECOND source of variance beside corpus sampling -- the conversion that produced the checkpoint -- and the published intervals do not contain it, because a bootstrap over source clusters resamples the corpus and holds the weights fixed.

That term has to be quantified (several siblings, not one) and disclosed wherever an interval is quoted, and any comparison BETWEEN checkpoints whose margin is of the same order as the sibling difference measured here has to be re-read as possibly a converter draw rather than a recipe effect.
what_it_does_not_license: It does not make any published number an overclaim, and it does not mean a rebuild is worse -- the sign of a single draw carries no information about which recipe is better.
One sibling gives the difference for one draw. It does not give the spread, which is what disclosure would need.

implications.both_were_publishable: Neither outcome was the hoped-for one. The two readings above were written into this tool before the score existed, and which one the receipt reports is decided by whether `paired.bootstrap_difference` brackets zero.
